sample1_text: I keep coming back to the idea that most of what I was afraid of at thirty never actually happened, and most of what did happen I never saw coming at all. I think I used to plan for certainty. Now I mostly just try to stay steady when things move, which is a different skill entirely, and one I'm still learning.
sample2_completions: The thing I'd tell someone new to this is you'll waste years trying to control what was never yours to control.
What actually annoys me is advice that assumes everyone's starting point looks the same.
If I'm honest, the hardest part was admitting I didn't know what I wanted, not just how to get it.
The way I'd explain this to a friend is growth is mostly just noticing the same mistake a little sooner each time.
render_input: It is important to note that personal growth represents a robust and transformative journey. Furthermore, one's ability to navigate uncertainty demonstrates a paramount life skill in today's ever-evolving landscape.

refinement.freetext: this sounds like a LinkedIn post about resilience, not how I actually think or write
